content.user_title: Build Typed UI Specifications with json-render
content.value_statement: AI-generated interfaces need consistent schemas, state bindings, and validation. This skill guides assistants through json-render core APIs for catalogs, prompts, streaming, and specification repair.
actual_capabilities: Guides schema and component catalog definitions using defineSchema, defineCatalog, and Zod property schemas.
Explains catalog prompts, user prompt builders, and patch, merge, and diff editing modes.
Shows how to compile streaming JSONL patches into progressively updated specifications.
Documents state bindings, computed properties, visibility conditions, watchers, and StateStore integration.
Explains field validation, structural specification checks, and lossy versus lossless repairs.
Guides experimental decision-model composition with atomic candidates, evaluator budgets, cancellation, and partial snapshots.
limitations: The skill contains documentation only; package installation, rendering components, and application integration remain separate work.
Experimental composition APIs are described as unreleased and may require a source build; their interfaces can change.
Experimental composition supports a narrower expression subset than general core specifications and requires application-supplied candidates.
Gateway evaluation requires server-side credentials and sends composition descriptions, prompts, topology, instructions, and explicit context to the evaluator.

use_cases.title: Define a reusable component catalog
use_cases.description: Frontend developers can structure component properties and catalog prompts for consistent AI-generated interfaces.

use_cases.title: Integrate progressive specification generation
use_cases.description: AI application engineers can plan JSONL streaming, refinement prompts, and validation before rendering generated specifications.

use_cases.title: Connect forms to shared state
use_cases.description: Design system maintainers can standardize form bindings, visibility rules, validation checks, and external state store adapters.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the core concepts
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain schemas, catalogs, specifications, and SpecStream in json-render. Use a small contact form as the example and identify the packages I need.

prompt_templates.title: Create a typed catalog
prompt_templates.prompt: Define a json-render schema and catalog for Button and TextInput components. Include Zod property constraints and show how catalog.prompt generates instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Review form bindings and repairs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my supplied form specification for state binding, visibility, and cross-field validation issues. Propose lossless repairs first and explain any changes requiring lossy fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan bounded experimental composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Design server-side experimental composition using my supplied catalog and atomic candidates. Include batch creation, sequential edits, evaluation budgets, cancellation, and partial snapshot handling. Identify evaluator data exposure and runtime action authorization requirements.

output_examples.input: Explain how to connect an email field to nested form state.
output: Bind the input value to the nested email path using a two-way state binding.
Read that same nested path in the submit action binding.
A bare email field name does not search nested form state.
Validate and authorize the action in the application handler.

output_examples.input: Describe a cautious repair workflow for a generated specification.
output: Run structural validation and inspect each reported issue.
Apply lossless fixes first and retry generation when required.
Review lossy fixes before pruning dangling child references.
Validate the repaired specification again before rendering.

output_examples.input: Explain what information the experimental evaluator receives.
output: The evaluator receives candidate descriptions, prompts, instructions, topology, and explicit context.
Initial state and raw property or binding values are not sent automatically.
Keep Gateway credentials on the server and exclude sensitive information from descriptions and context.

best_practices: Validate generated specifications and review lossy repairs before rendering; separately validate and authorize runtime actions.
Keep evaluator credentials server-side and minimize sensitive data in descriptions, prompts, and explicit context.
Pin experimental package versions when published, set evaluation limits, and supply an overall abort signal.
anti_patterns: Treating schema validation as proof of semantic completeness or permission to execute actions.
Using repeat, watch, computed, template, or conditional properties in the experimental composition subset.
Assuming a catalog alone supplies configured candidate values, bindings, and rendering implementations.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill provides Markdown guidance and TypeScript examples rather than a standalone executable.

faq.question: Does this skill install json-render or render an interface?
faq.answer: No. It guides core API usage; your project must provide dependencies, rendering components, and application integration.

faq.question: Are the experimental composition APIs stable?
faq.answer: No. The documentation describes them as unreleased, requiring a source build until publication. Experimental exports and types may change in any release.

faq.question: What information leaves the application during Gateway evaluation?
faq.answer: Descriptions, prompts, instructions, topology, and explicit context reach the evaluator. Initial state and raw property or binding values are not sent automatically.

faq.question: What should I check when form values do not resolve?
faq.answer: Use explicit paths for nested state and bind the natural input value property. A bare field name does not search nested form objects.

faq.question: Does specification validation secure action execution?
faq.answer: No. Applications must validate and authorize actions at runtime. Built-ins without parameter schemas receive name validation only during experimental composition.
